title: Teledermatology & lesion photography
summary: How store-and-forward teledermatology works in the UK, the three images every lesion referral needs (regional, close-up with scale, dermoscopic), what it does well, and its pitfalls.

glance.think: Referring a skin lesion through a teledermatology or advice-and-guidance service.
glance.engine: Images and history are triaged by a dermatologist, who can discharge, advise, book surgery directly or fast-track.
glance.backbone: Three views: regional for location, close-up with a ruler, and a polarised in-focus dermoscopic image; full history including change and risk factors; consent.
glance.never_miss: Poor-quality images, missing dermoscopy, lesions on the scalp, genitals or nails, and delay in a suspected melanoma pathway.

what: Remote assessment of skin lesions from. In the UK it is mostly **store-and-forward** (asynchronous) **advice-and-guidance** or **2WW triage**, using dermoscopic + close-up + regional photographs.
features: NHS England's **A teledermatology roadmap** (2023) describes models:

list: referral triage (images attached to all 2WW skin referrals)
community "image capture hubs" with trained medical photographers
AI-assisted triage (HTG746; see *Recognition, diagnostic accuracy, dermoscopy and AI*).

features.h: Image standards (BAD/PCDS/Primary Care Dermatology quality standards)

list: **Three views:** a regional/whole-site image (anatomical location), a close-up with a **ruler/scale**, and a **dermoscopic image** (polarised, in focus, the whole lesion in view).

Good lighting, no flash glare, a plain background, a labelled patient ID, consent, and secure NHS-approved systems (**no personal phones/WhatsApp** without an approved app and policy). Include history (duration, change, symptoms, 7-point score, risk factors, Fitzpatrick type).

features: For lesion triage, accuracy is comparable to face-to-face assessment for many lesions when dermoscopic images are of good quality. It reduces unnecessary face-to-face appointments and speeds up the management of cancers. Image quality is the main failure mode. Darker skin types are under-represented in training.
Nodular/amelanotic melanoma can be under-called on. Teledermatology must not delay a 2WW-meeting referral; where a pathway uses, they **accompany** the urgent referral rather than replace it.

list: Learn the local teledermatology pathway and image capture standards. An IP in a PCN may capture images if trained.
**[Case 3](condition:melanoma):** a lesion changing over 2 years (change = 2, plus any other feature) → 2WW referral with. The specialist arranges excision biopsy within the pathway.

red_flags: Teledermatology must not delay a **suspected cancer pathway** referral: if images are poor, refer face to face.
pearls: Tell the patient that photos may be reviewed by a specialist first and they may be booked straight for surgery. Get consent for image storage.
